item.title: Bad Bunny’s Ex-Girlfriend Can Keep Suing Him Over Voice Memo on ‘Un Verano Sin Ti’ Track, Court Rules
item.description:
Here's a short and engaging podcast script based on the article:
[Intro music]
Host: "Welcome to Trending on Billboard, the podcast where we dive into the latest music news and updates. I'm your host, [Name]. Today, we're talking about a major development in a lawsuit involving Latin superstar Bad Bunny. Let's get into it."
[Music transition]
Host: "The Supreme Court of Puerto Rico has ruled that Bad Bunny's ex-girlfriend, Carliz De La Cruz Hernández, can continue suing the singer for featuring her voice on his chart-topping album Un Verano Sin Ti without permission. The voice in question says the phrase 'Bad Bunny baby', which was recorded by De La Cruz Hernández back in 2015 at Bad Bunny's request."
[Short music clip from Bad Bunny's song]
Host: "According to the court, De La Cruz Hernández can pursue claims under Puerto Rico's right of publicity law, which protects an individual's voice from being used without their consent in a commercial setting. Interestingly, the court found that the use of her voice on the song 'Dos Mil 16' was a form of advertising, as it fueled fan speculation about Bad Bunny's romantic relationship and drove album sales."
[Music transition]
Host: "The lawsuit will now move forward, with De La Cruz Hernández allowed to pursue claims over the use of her voice on 'Dos Mil 16', as well as copyright claims for allegedly infringing her rights to the 'Bad Bunny baby' voice memo. This is a significant development in the case, and we'll be keeping an eye on it as it unfolds."
[Outro music]
Host: "That's all for today's episode of Trending on Billboard. Thanks for tuning in, and we'll catch you on the next one."
